processIssues.description: Systemic session-to-feature mismatch across all 9 features. Every worker session implemented a different feature than assigned, creating a cascading chain of misattributed handoffs. Despite this, all features were correctly implemented — the code exists and all tests pass.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add coding convention: 'When an ORM model exists in core/database.py for a table, skill handlers MUST use that ORM model for queries instead of raw SQL via text(). Raw SQL should only be used when no ORM model exists for the target table.'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: social_media, market_intelligence, and email_marketing skills all use raw SQL text() for DB operations despite having ORM models defined in core/database.py. This inconsistency was flagged in 3 separate reviews.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add coding convention: 'Remove unused imports before committing. Run a quick import check (e.g., `grep -n ^from handler.py` and verify each import is used) as part of the pre-commit checklist.'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Unused imports found in calendar/handler.py (text, Any/Dict/List/Optional), backup_automation/handler.py (glob, Path, Any/Dict/List/Optional), and research_agent/handler.py (text). Flagged in 3 separate reviews.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: The backend-worker skill's TDD 'Write Tests FIRST (Red Phase)' step should be modified to acknowledge that for brand-new file creation, test-first may not be practical since there's nothing to import yet. Suggest: 'For new modules, you may create the module skeleton (class definition with pass) first, then write tests, then implement. For upgrades to existing code, write tests first.'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: Multiple worker transcripts show workers creating implementation before tests. The skill-hot-reload worker explicitly noted this in skillFeedback. The skill-integration-tests feature (test-only) also doesn't fit the TDD pattern.

suggestedGuidanceUpdates.suggestion: Add to Architecture Notes: 'The watchdog library (>=6.0) is used for skill hot-reload. A SkillFileWatcher daemon thread starts automatically on app startup and monitors backend/skills/ for manifest.yaml and handler.py changes. Invalid changes are caught and logged without crashing the watcher.'
suggestedGuidanceUpdates.evidence: The hot-reload feature adds an automatic background thread that operators should know about. Currently undocumented in AGENTS.md architecture notes.

rejectedObservations.reason: Already addressed in suggestedGuidanceUpdates as a skill procedure change recommendation. The observation that workers don't follow TDD strictly is valid but is better addressed by updating the procedure rather than flagging it as a convention violation.
